Value = the model's pick at a price that pays more than its chance is worth: model chance × decimal odds − 1, so a positive figure already clears the book's margin. Anytime Touchdown — 273 players
Probability that the player scores a rushing or receiving touchdown, assuming he plays — the same basis on which these markets settle, so a quarterback counts for his rushing touchdowns (each team's expected starter is listed; for him Opp/gm is carries). Driven by projected volume and the market's implied team total, and for quarterbacks also goal-line carries and how often they have scored; otherwise the red zone and goal-line columns are context, not model inputs, because adding them was tested and gained nothing. Gm is games played this season. Probabilities above about 45% have run a few points high in backtesting. Players ruled out or doubtful, on injured reserve, waived or left off the game-day active list are dropped as soon as that becomes public, which lifts the share of listed players who actually take a snap from 83% to 97%. Q marks a questionable player and Q·DNP one who also missed practice all week — those have played only about half the time.
Receiving Yards — 235 players
Projected yards assuming the player plays, with the historically observed rate of clearing each line for a projection of this size. Over probabilities are fit on prior seasons only and run about 1-2 points high.
No leakage. Each prediction uses only games that had finished before that game's kickoff, plus completed prior seasons. Until kickoff it updates automatically as new results arrive; at kickoff it is locked permanently and never recomputed. Both model regimes and the confidence curve are fit only on 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025.
Model. This week uses EPA plus this season's point differential.
Confidence is the historically observed hit rate for predictions of this size, fit as a smooth curve. Games near the bottom really are coin tosses.
Caveat. This model does not beat the betting market: walk-forward over 2017-2025 it called 64.6% of games straight up (Brier 0.221) against 67.1% (Brier 0.210) for the closing moneyline favourite, and it has no edge against the spread.

Anytime Touchdown — top 100 of 1396 players
Chance the player scores a rushing or receiving touchdown, assuming he plays. Built from his carries, catches, yards and touchdowns this season (last season counts as two games early on), his share of his team's touches and the scoring matchup, all as of kickoff; fit on prior seasons only. Out of sample on 2025 it was well calibrated: players given 26% scored 27% of the time; chances above 60% ran a few points high. Listed players touched the ball in their team's previous game. Fair odds = 1 ÷ chance.
No leakage. Every rating uses only games finished before that game's kickoff, plus completed prior seasons. The rating-to-points mapping and the confidence curve are fit on 2016-2025 alone (7,056 games). Until kickoff a prediction updates as results arrive; at kickoff it is locked permanently and never recomputed.
Model. A team's rating blends its games so far this season with a preseason prior. The prior is fit on prior seasons from last year's rating, the four-year recruiting composite, and how much on-field production the roster kept or imported through the transfer portal. Early weeks lean on the prior; by November it is almost all on-field EPA.
Accuracy. Walk-forward over 2018-2025 (5,620 FBS matchups) the model called 71.6% correctly with an average margin error of 13.4 points. Recruiting and transfer terms are worth about a point of accuracy overall and three in the opening weeks. Since v2 the rating-to-points slope is steeper in weeks 1-4, which fixed the early-season underconfidence (it said 68% in weeks 1-2 and won 75%).
Scope. FBS against FBS only. Games against FCS opponents still inform the ratings but are not shown, because a 99% pick tells you nothing.

Anytime goalscorer — 85 skaters
Probability the skater records at least one goal, assuming he dresses. His own scoring rate shrunk toward the positional base rate. Shots on goal and time on ice were tested as multipliers and made it worse, so they are out. Calibrated to within a point in every bucket over 2024-25 and 2025-26.
No leakage. Ratings use only games finished before the slate, and the rating-to-goals mapping plus the confidence curve are fit on earlier seasons alone (7,667 games).
Accuracy. 57.97% of games called correctly [55.7, 59.5], average margin error 2.09 goals, on 5,125 games. Confidence is calibrated: 54.7% at the flat end rising to 67.3% at the top. Hockey is the hardest of these leagues to predict and the market itself sits near 58%.

First basket — 148 players
First FG excludes free throws; first score counts them. 99.9% of first field goals are scored by a starter, and a free throw opens the game 7.1% of the time. Each number is the man's own history shrunk toward his positional rate, times his share of his team's last 20 games — so it is the chance he takes the first basket, not the chance he takes it if he starts. One first basket is scored per game, so where both fives are known the ten are scaled to sum to 100%: built separately they came to 103.8% on average and as much as 128%, which reads as value against a book price that is not there. Once a line-up is posted, about an hour before tip-off, the five are taken as given and nobody else is listed. Rosters come from the team feed, because the season files that record who played are published a season behind. Walk-forward on 1,479 games from 2023 the top pick hit 12.9%, against 10% for picking a starter at random, and a game's stated chances sum to 1.02. A team strength term was tested and earned zero weight.
No leakage. Ratings use only games finished before the slate; the mapping and the confidence curve are fit on earlier seasons alone (12,000 games).
Accuracy. 65.1% of games called correctly, average margin error 10.9 points. Rest is in the model: a team on zero or one day's rest averages 1.95 points worse, against plus 0.43 on two or more, which is a larger swing than the 2.14-point home advantage.

Game outcomes — close games first
Rated on margin over a two-season window. Across 23,282 past games it called 71% of sides against 64% for always taking the home team, and its stated confidence matches what happened to within a point or two. Two honest limits: a game projected inside three points is close to a coin toss (55%), and nothing here knows who is injured — college basketball publishes no injury report and ESPN carries no pre-game lineups, so a side missing a starter looks like any other side.
